questions.q: Which workload is the best fit for a batch endpoint?
options: Scoring two million customers overnight with no one waiting on any single answer
Returning a fraud decision while a customer waits at checkout
Answering one chatbot message in under 200 milliseconds
Serving a live dashboard that refreshes every second
questions.explain: Batch endpoints suit large, slow, asynchronous scoring with no low-latency requirement. Anything where a person or app is waiting belongs on a real-time endpoint.

questions.q: What does a batch endpoint receive when you invoke it?
options: The full dataset embedded in the request body
A pointer to data in storage, such as a folder or data asset
Only a single row of features
A trained model file to score itself
questions.explain: Batch endpoints take pointers to data (datastores, data assets or storage accounts) and run an asynchronous job over it.

questions.q: In a batch scoring script, where should you load the model?
options: Inside run(), fresh for every file
In a separate notebook, then paste the weights into the request
In init(), which runs once per worker process
Nowhere — Azure loads it automatically for every script
questions.explain: init() is for costly one-time setup such as loading the model. run(mini_batch) is called repeatedly and should reuse the loaded model.

questions.q: You test your script locally with 5 input files and a mini-batch size of 2. How many times is run() called?
questions.explain: Files are split into mini-batches of 2, 2 and 1, so run() is called three times, exactly as in the local test.

questions.q: Why is putting deployments behind one batch endpoint useful for model upgrades?
options: It lets you switch the default deployment without changing how consumers invoke the endpoint
It makes the model more accurate automatically
It removes the need for any compute cluster
It forces every consumer to update their code
questions.explain: The endpoint is a stable interface. You can add a new deployment, test it, and promote it to default without breaking callers.
